chapter_theme: The cipher followed as a route through the body: the way of Paychalur, the horn, the bow's curve, the whirl, the crown, where the red flame rises past the moon and nada runs. The chapter's two plain verses (1334, 1335) give the same route in yoga's own words: lotus posture, the root fire roused by the wind, the nine gates sealed, the spine, the six centres, nectar drunk at the moon, the good yogi who reaches the crown and comes down. It closes on where life withdraws, on release and siddhi as a pair, and on the one letter beyond which there is nothing to say.
structure_note: 1314 to 1333 are the cipher, mostly chains of locatives ending in சிவாயமே or மோனமே, with a few attacks on seekers and boasters (1316, 1318) and two stanzas on the breath's birth and death in the body (1328, 1333) that share a formula. 1334 and 1335 are the plain yoga verses, and 1336 to 1338 generalise: the hidden gate, mukti and siddhi, the one letter.

1314.reading: Nada rising like a mill from the five horns; with the bud the flower blossomed, purity attained; when the red flame rose, the teacher slipped loose at once and became the five elements: the silence that flew away.
1314.nuance: ஆலை is a sugar mill or press, so the sound rises as a mill's does. தேசிகன், the teacher or the dweller, may be the guru or the indwelling life; its slipping loose and becoming the five elements reads as the body's dissolution at the flame's rise, or as the self's release. The two readings differ on who leaves.

1315.reading: On the sudden horn, in the nature of the tattvas, in the striking 'ā', in the 'ū' where Hara dwelt, in the grove called 'iduthi', in the triple flame that stood, nada ran saying 'naduthi' and settled well.
1315.nuance: The -துதி words (சடுதி, அடுதி, இடுதி, நடுதி) are rhyme-makers whose sense I cannot fix; the letters ஆ and ஊ are cipher like கூ and கீ. The triple flame is sun, moon and fire on the usual reading. The event is nada running and settling.

1316.reading: The silence of Vishnu who settles, the silence where Hara dwelt, the silence of the elements composed, the silence held, the speed that owns the eyelid, the silence of the shining crown: men who know themselves do not look upon the corpse.
1316.nuance: சடம், the inert thing, is the body; those who know themselves (தமையறிந்த) do not attend to it. இமையும் கொண்ட வேகம், the speed that has the eyelid, is the flash within a blink. The silences are listed as in 1303.

1317.reading: In the way of Paychalur, in the whirl where the Supreme dwelt, at the tip of the ripening horn, on the mountain where the fruit is: what is it that smells so? The expanse rests here; the light that stands pressing, drawing breath from breath.
1317.nuance: பாய்ச்சலூர், the town of leaping or flowing, recurs in 1328 and 1333 and is cipher for the breath's course or the central channel, as tradition takes it, not a place. மூச்சினோடு மூச்சை வாங்கு, drawing breath by breath, is the one plain phrase. The question ஏதடா asks what the fragrance or stench at the fruit is.

1318.reading: A few are those who seek 'light, light' and fail; a few are the men who seek 'the First, the First'; a few are the idle who say 'disputant, disputant'; the whole flame stands as right, right, right, right.
1318.nuance: Three kinds of seeker, each சிலவரே, a few, against the one whole flame (முழுச்சுடர்) that stands as நீதி. The verse puts even the seekers of light among those who fail; the flame is not reached by naming it.

1319.reading: Becoming flame, rising there, the time it became incense; before earth and sky were made one as a trouble, the Beginning that stood spreading became the five elements and stood as prowess, dense through all the cosmos.
1319.nuance: A cosmogony: the Beginning spreads into the five elements and fills every world. ஆண்மை (prowess, manliness) is the odd word, as in 1298 and 1307; here it may mean the sovereign self. இடரதாய், as a trouble, is unexplained.

1320.reading: Men on earth who see and know the light that stood, their eyes cooled, and go about in love: they will see the vision at the upper point of the throat; the withering gone, the ... surging, nada too rejoices.
1320.nuance: கண்டம், the throat, is the fifth centre; the vision is placed above it. காதலுற்று, in love, is the condition of the seers. நாலை in line 4 is obscure, perhaps a misprint for வாலை (the maiden) or நாளை.

1321.reading: The red flame of shining silence, the light that drained, and nada, crying out like tanks in the space emptied of Karuvur; the nature that spread with no fear at all; the lamp that is the Lady, trembling and crying out at the pleasures.
1321.nuance: கருவூர், the embryo town, is the womb or the body's seat (compare 1332); the space emptied of it is beyond birth. நங்கை, the Lady, is Shakti as the lamp. கயங்கள்போலக் கதறி and நயங்கள் கோவென்று are obscure; the stanza's sense beyond its nouns is not recoverable by me.

1322.reading: At the tip of the lamp's crown, in the channel of the sun's light, in the 'kū' where anger changes, in the fire that stood boiling, the subtlety settled in the corner of heat, and the release that is a curse: cut off, it shines.
1322.nuance: திவாகரம் is the sun's light. சாபமான மோட்சம், release that is a curse, is the hard phrase: either release bound up with the curse of birth, or release that is itself a curse to one who wants more, or two items in the list, curse and release. தடிந்து, cut off, may govern either.

1323.reading: The teacher whirled in the maiden of the triple point; in the maiden with a guise, in the corner where the vast dwelt, at the gate filled with the beloved moonrise, the silence that spread stood fanning and fanning.
1323.nuance: திரிமுனை, the triple point, is where the three channels meet on tradition's reading. சந்திரோதயம், moonrise, is the yogic moon at the head. தேசிகன் again may be the guru or the indwelling self; வேசம், guise, is what the maiden puts on.

1324.reading: Nandi who stood wearied on the silence of the inner lotus; becoming 'kī' with a hiccup in the middle of the bow's curve; the red flame that hurried as if thorns were packed in it; the vision that stood driving on like heaps of liquor.
1324.nuance: Nandi is Siva, as in Tirumular. விக்கல், the hiccup, may be the catch of the held breath. The similes of thorns and heaps of liquor are not ones I can place; கட்குவைகள் may be corrupt. The bow's curve is the brow.

1325.reading: From the navel by the way of the whirl to the middle of the crown, the red flame that leapt past the moon's light and the organs; becoming the bond in the bow's curve, the magic of the five elements; standing like a drop in 'kī', it said 'kīch mūch'.
1325.nuance: The clearest route in the chapter: navel, whirl, crown. கரணம், the organs, are the inner instruments the flame passes. கிந்து is probably விந்து (bindu). கீச்சுமூச்சு is onomatopoeia for a squeak and a breath, with மூச்சு the breath itself; the verse ends in the body's own noise.

1326.reading: With the breath called 'secchai', the letters SI and VA stood fresh: the nature of the supreme space. In the 'ū' of desire, in the 'ī' that rose there, in the angle of the crown Sivayam rose.
1326.nuance: சிகாரமும் வகாரமும் are the letters சி and வ, the first two of சிவாய, so the five letters are built from the breath. செச்சை is vermilion or a flower-name and here names a breath. ஊ and ஈ join the cipher syllables; பச்சை, green or fresh, is the state of the letters.

1327.reading: In the six-cornered angle, in the ninefold that is set, so that the Lady's navel is discerned saying 'thāru'; the silence the five held there saying 'kūru'; what stood holding a vulture spread: Sivayam.
1327.nuance: ஆறுமூலைக் கோணம், the six-cornered figure, is the hexagram of the yantras or the six centres; ஒன்பதாத்து is obscure, perhaps the nine gates. நாவி is navel or musk. பாறு is a vulture or spreading; the last line is not recoverable by me.

1328.reading: It flew, when it was milked, by the way of Paychalur: what was born was breath, not female nor male. Did it renounce, did it excel, did it become pure and lofty? Not at the moment of death: Sivayam shines then too.
1328.nuance: The plain claim in line 2 is that what is born in the body's way is the breath, which has no sex. கறந்தபோது, when milked, is odd; it may be the drawing of the breath. The last line can be 'not only then' or 'not then but now'; the formula returns in 1333 with துறந்தபோது for கறந்தபோது.

1329.reading: In the space where grace was, in the darkness where the sun stood, in the whirl where the substance was, in the way that rose turning over, in the phase where clarity was, in the net where one stood bewildered: from the way where the guru was, it became 'ū' and 'ī'.
1329.nuance: Six locatives, each a quality placed in a space (grace, darkness, substance, clarity, bewilderment), then the guru's way as the source of the two syllables. The sun standing in darkness is the hidden light of the body on the coded reading. கலை is phase or art.

1330.reading: The Beginning settled in the one letter: with song and on this earth there is no seeing and knowing it; it became itself and itself; in the evening and morning that were composed it was like millet and its change: Sivayam.
1330.nuance: ஓர் எழுத்து, the one letter, is Om on the usual reading. தானும் தானும் ஆனதே, it became itself and itself, is identity without a second. ஏனலோடு மாறுபோல், like millet and its exchange, is unexplained; it may be the field's change from seed to crop or a barter image.

1331.reading: The flood the river took, the god established there, the rain the thicket took, the distance that shone, the silence that took pride, the shining inner lotus: in the contrary 'ū' it died away: Sivayam.
1331.nuance: The list ends with a death (மடிந்ததே) rather than a rising, as if the inner lotus and its silence are themselves passed. மாறுகொண்ட ஊ, the ū that turned contrary, may be the breath reversed. The images of flood, rain and distance are not ones tradition explains for this verse.

1332.reading: In the angle seen at the gate, the five shining ones dwelling; seeing the shadow and leaning on it, abiding as the head-king; the bee of the body having seen it, having gone there to Karuvur, having gone saying 'it will leap': it flew: Sivayam.
1332.nuance: காயவண்டு, the bee of the body, is the life entering a body, and கருவூர், the embryo town, the womb: the stanza tells the soul's descent into birth, seeing a shadow, leaning on it, ruling as head, then flying off. The five who dwell are the elements or senses. The reading of the whole as birth is mine; the words are a sequence of participles.

1333.reading: It flew, when it renounced, by the way of Paychalur; it forgot, settled in the hand of the warriors who seized it; it was born; at the moment of death, in the 'kī' without harm, the silence that excelled became clear: Sivayam.
1333.nuance: The formula of 1328 with the verbs changed: flew, forgot, was born, and at death the silence cleared. வாணர், the warriors or the Vanar, who seize may be the senses or Death's men; பீடிடாமல், without harm or without seat, is unclear. The pair of stanzas tells the breath's whole career from entry to exit.

1334.reading: Seating the body in the lotus posture, rousing the fire at the root with the wind, sealing the gates, five and four, with the final mudra, it goes by the root vina-staff past the lotus temple and through the root nadi.
1334.nuance: The one verse in these chapters in yoga's open vocabulary. மூல அனல் is the root fire, kundalini in later usage, raised by மாருதம், the breath; the nine gates (five and four) are the body's openings, closed by mudra; வீணாதண்டு, the vina's staff, is the spine; முளரி ஆலயம், the lotus temple, is the heart or a centre passed on the way. What goes is the breath or the fire; the subject is unstated.

1335.reading: Beginning at the feet and up to the crown, crossing the six great grounds, our primal light that passed beyond the space beyond; drinking nectar at the eye of the lord of the stars, in the joy of true knowledge, the yogi who strikes the crown and comes down is the good yogi.
1335.nuance: ஆறுமா நிலம், the six great grounds, are the six centres; உடுபதி, the lord of the stars, is the moon, whose nectar the yogi drinks at the head, as in Tirumular. இறங்குகின்ற, coming down, is the mark of the good yogi: he reaches the crown and returns, rather than staying.

1336.reading: 'Is it inside or outside, the place where life withdraws? You must come slowly, draw near and ask', you say. When what is and what is born coincide, that is nada; open the thief's gate and see, men.
1336.nuance: The questioners want the place of life's withdrawal located and taught; the answer refuses inside and outside and gives a condition instead, the coincidence of being and birth (உள்ளதும் பிறப்பதும்), which is nada. கள்ளவாசல், the thief's gate, is the hidden door, which tradition takes as the opening of the central channel.

1337.reading: Release and siddhi are a pair; the Murti who embraces; the five senses that arose otherwise become ... in that sense; Father, eternal one, poison-throated one: with love, every day, recite and know and realise him within the heart.
1337.nuance: முத்தி சித்தி தொந்தமாம், release and attainment are joined, is the claim of the opening: the Siddhar's powers and his liberation come together. Line 2 (ஆகுமத்தி அப்புலன்) is garbled. The close is plain devotion: daily recitation with love, and inner knowing.

1338.reading: Becoming three and two and five, the gods strove and rose; becoming three and two as five, all the worlds strove; the mother who bore and the father being the nada that moves: there is nothing to say beyond the one letter that appears.
1338.nuance: மூன்றிரண்டும் ஐந்துமாய், three and two making five, may be the five letters, the five elements or three gunas with two more; the verse gives only the counts. Mother and father as nada make sound the parent of gods and worlds; the one letter that appears is Om on the usual reading, and the last line ends the argument: beyond it nothing is sayable.

links.note: Tirumular's eight siddhis come when the fire at the root of the central channel drives the sun and lets the moon drink; Sivavakkiyar rouses the root fire with the wind, seals the gates and sends it up the spine through the root nadi.

Both send the mantra or the fire up the வீணாதண்டு, the vina's staff: 1381 has the mantra blossoming in the eight letters and passing through the vina-staff, 1334 the roused fire going by the root vina-staff past the lotus temple.

Pambatti takes the thought standing at the root place through the suzhumunai to the bindu circle above; Sivavakkiyar takes the root fire by the spine through the root nadi, with the same posture-and-breath method.

Tirumular's Siva-yogis raise the fire, seal the whirl and drink the nectar of the full moon step by step; Sivavakkiyar's good yogi crosses the six centres and drinks nectar at the eye of the lord of stars.

Tirumular answers the inside-or-outside question with a mirror: the Lord is as each says. Sivavakkiyar refuses the question for the place where life withdraws and replaces it with a condition and an act: when being and birth coincide it is nada, so open the hidden gate and look.

Tirumular says no one sees the one letter in the sky and the world knows only letters on water; Sivavakkiyar says the Beginning settled in the one letter cannot be seen or known on this earth or in song.
Tirumular sets the eight siddhis beside the cutting of birth and credits both to grace; Sivavakkiyar opens with release and siddhi as a bound pair and ends in daily loving recitation.

Both count the Lord's letters: Tirumular's one letter becomes the world, two join as two, three make the light; Sivavakkiyar's three and two and five make gods and worlds, and the one letter that appears is the end of speech.

new_concepts.gloss: vaasi: the breath as the thing practised, ridden or raised in Siddhar yoga; also the horse, and a play on the syllables of சிவாய
new_concepts.label_source: the verses use the word (1291 வாசிஏறி); declared also in ch068

new_concepts.gloss: the whirl-point: the central channel and its opening at the brow or crown, where the breath of sun and moon becomes one
new_concepts.label_source: the verses use சுழி and சுழிவழி for it (1317, 1325, 1329); சுழுமுனை is the standard form; declared also in ch068

new_concepts.gloss: the subtle: the hidden inner thing or secret the Siddhar points to and the reciter misses, named but not explained
new_concepts.label_source: the verses use the word (1322); declared also in ch068

new_concepts.gloss: the maiden: the young goddess as the power in the body, the flame in the wick, in Siddhar cipher the kundalini or the breath at the whirl-point
new_concepts.label_source: the verses use the word (1323); declared also in ch068

source_issues: 1320 line 4 நாலை is obscure; probably a misprint for வாலை or நாளை.
1325 line 1 மத்தயில் is a misprint for மத்தியில்; line 4 கிந்து is probably விந்து.
1337 line 2 ஆகுமத்தி அப்புலன் is garbled and gives no construable sense.
1327 line 1 ஒன்பதாத்திலே and 1324 line 4 கட்குவைகள் are words I cannot identify and may be corrupt.
1328 and 1333 share a formula (பறந்ததே ... பாய்ச்சலூர் வழியிலே ... இறந்தபோதில்) with the verbs changed; they are variants of one stanza or a deliberate pair.
The new concepts vaasi, suzhumunai, sootcham and vaalai are declared in both ch068 and ch069 so that each file passes check on its own; they should be merged once into concepts.json.
